```python
from torch_geometric.nn import HGTConv
import torch

m = HGTConv(16, 16, ([], []))
s = torch.jit.script(m)
```

items.title: Incorrect data in QM9 dataset
items.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Hello developers,
I found that the implementation of QM9 in PyG version 2.6.1 contains incorrect data.
- First, for the edge_attrs of all molecules, no aromatic bond type is assigned to any bond.
- Second, I found some bonds defined in the gdb9.sdf file that are too long to be considered valid bonds. For example, gdb_1150 has a C-C bond with a bond length of 1.87 Å, which is abnormal for an optimized molecule. In the corresponding part of the .sdf file, an extra bond is defined for atom 2 and 4. This violates the basic chemical rules.
- Additionally, the method to obtain SMILES strings is also problematic. Since the topological relations are mistakenly defined in the .sdf file, the SMILES obtained based on such relations may not be correct. For example, in gdb_133408, the original SMILES should be OC1=CC(=N)C(F)=NN1 while the processed one becomes [H][N-]C1=C(F)N=[N+]([H])C(O[H])=C1[H]. Even though the latter is a valid SMILES, it still indicates a different set of bond types.

This incorrect data will certainly undermine the reliability of the models trained on this implementation of QM9.

There is much more incorrect data in the .sdf file. My suggestions are: 1. obtain the topological information (edge_index and edge_attr) using other robust methods, and 2. use the original SMILES strings instead of the newly generated ones. It is hard to notice these mistakes, but they may cause real trouble since this is one of the most popular datasets for benchmarking.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On a freshly installed Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) [VM] (_version details available below_), I followed these steps to install python 3.11:
```Bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade

sudo apt install -y python3.11 python3.11-venv python3.11-dev python3.11-distutils
```
and create a virtual environment:
```Bash
python3.11 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
```
Inside virtual environment, I installed pytorch based on [pytorch docs](https://pytorch.org/get-started/previous-versions/#linux-and-windows-5):
```Bash
pip install torch==2.4.0 torchvision==0.19.0 torchaudio==2.4.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124
```
and then based on [PyG docs](https://pytorch-geometric.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install/installation.html#quick-start):
```Bash
pip install torch_geometric
```
Up until this point everything is fine. Running:
```python
import torch_geometric
print(f'version: {torch_geometric.__version__}')"
```
returns: ```version: 2.6.1```. But after installing optional dependencies using: 

```Bash
pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse torch_cluster torch_spline_conv -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.4.1+cu124.html
```

```python
import torch_geometric
```
returns: 
```
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
Turns out this issue also happens while importing ```torch_sparse``` but importing ```pyg_lib```, ```torch_scatter```, ```torch_cluster```, and ```torch_spline_conv``` works fine.

I believe this issue might not be new as I found related examples in [pytorch_sparse issues](https://github.com/rusty1s/pytorch_sparse/issues/228) and [pytorch_geometric issues](https://github.com/pyg-team/pytorch_geometric/issues/6878) as well, but those issues were most likely caused by incompatible dependency versions.

items.title: Error in splitting indices in `distributed_sampling.py`
items.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The example code `examples/multi_gpu/distributed_sampling.py` of using distributed sampling with multiple GPUs has a bug in the splitting of the indices.

```python
# Split indices into `world_size` many chunks:
train_idx = data.train_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=False).view(-1)
train_idx = train_idx.split(train_idx.size(0) // world_size)[rank]
```
This code does floor division to split `train_idx` to `world_size` chunks, but since this is a floor division, it can create `world_size + 1` chunks. To fix this issue, use the ceiling division.

```python
import math

# Split indices into `world_size` many chunks:
train_idx = data.train_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=False).view(-1)
train_idx = train_idx.split(math.ceil(train_idx.size(0) / world_size))[rank]
```

This ensures that we have `world_size` chunks.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Hi,

I get the error` TypeError: forward() got multiple values for argument 'data'`, when trying to pass the whole `data` object as an additional argument. In this toy example, I show that the data object is to be forwarded to the model instead of separate attributes. In the real model, the data object contains more than just `x` and `edge_index`, and passing every argument separately is not efficient. The explainer forwards, expected `x` and `edge_index `to be explicitly passed, while the model expects the whole data object. How to solve this?

Thanks

Reproducible code: 

```
from torch_geometric.data import Data
import torch

import torch.nn as nn
from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

import torch.optim as optim
import torch.nn.functional as F

from torch_geometric.explain import CaptumExplainer, Explainer

x = torch.tensor([[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5]], dtype=torch.float)  # 4 nodes

edge_index = torch.tensor([
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 3],  # Source nodes
    [1, 2, 3, 0, 2, 1]   # Target nodes
], dtype=torch.long)

y = torch.tensor([0, 1, 0, 1], dtype=torch.long)

data = Data(x=x, edge_index=edge_index, y=y)


class ToyGCN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim):
        super(ToyGCN, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = GCNConv(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.conv2 = GCNConv(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()

    def forward(self, data):
        x, edge_index = data.x, data.edge_index
        x = self.conv1(x, edge_index)
        x = self.relu(x)
        x = self.conv2(x, edge_index)
        return x

input_dim = data.x.shape[1]

optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)

    optimizer.zero_grad()
    out = model(data)
```
